transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Kaur (Redwood CSM), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Maria Lopez (AxiomWave), Jon Park (AxiomWave), Ethan Chu (AxiomWave PM)

Summary (auto):
Quick kickoff/check-in to align on access, staging environment, security requirements and success metrics for AxiomWave's pilot of Redwood's inference platform. Primary topics: VPC/on‑prem options, SOC2/KMS requirements, rollout plan, staging benchmark and next steps.

Topics:
- Access and networking (VPC peering, firewall rules)
- Security docs and compliance (SOC2, KMS, data retention)
- Staging vs prod plan and test dataset
- Pilot success criteria and timelines
- Operational handoffs and runbook distribution

Action items (captured): see metadata list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Mercer: ok, um hi everyone thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood inference, i'm the AE on this, with priya and diego, uh we'll run through a quick intake and then hand to diego for the technical bits, can you do quick intros from axiomwave?
[00:12] Maria Lopez: hi all, maria here, head of ml at axiomwave, we're kicking off a small pilot to move some document summarization and retrieval augmented generation into prod, excited to see the runbook, thanks for setting this up,
[00:22] Jon Park: jon, infra lead, i'll own VPC/peering and network config, also want to understand credentialing and key mgmt,
[00:30] Ethan Chu: ethan product, i'll track success metrics and stakeholder comms,
[00:34] Priya Kaur: awesome thanks all, the objective today is to collect the remaining access items, align on staging env, and confirm timelines for the pilot, we expect to hand you the runbook and security pack after this call,
[00:45] Diego Ramos: hey team, diego here, i'll cover the staging benchmark, latency expectations and sampling config, and i'll do a quick checklist for KV cache and batching settings,
[00:56] Maria Lopez: quick note — we do have a strict retention policy for customer PII, so redwood private or dedicated options were the ones we flagged, we want to confirm how logs and prompts are stored,
[01:08] Alex Mercer: yes understood, we can go over private deployment options — i want to mention that our private control plane supports customer KMS integration and optional on‑prem packages; diego will detail the differences between Dedicated vs Private since there's overlap and sometimes the names get mixed in notes,
[01:24] Diego Ramos: right, basically Dedicated is reserved capacity in our cloud with data isolation, private is the vpc/on‑prem variant where you can bring your own KMS, some customers call it "redwood privat" in notes — lol,
[01:34] Jon Park: ha, we saw that in docs, ok so network — we can do VPC peering into your staging subnet, we need IP ranges and peering guide, plus whether there are any port requirements beyond 443,
[01:46] Alex Mercer: good Q, standard ports are 443 and some grpc endpoints for high throughput, i'll share a short network checklist, priya will include the cidr examples,
[01:56] Priya Kaur: i'll attach a template for peering and a checklist for firewall rules, also SAML/SO sign‑on flows, we'll need an initial list of service accounts and IAM roles,
[02:08] Ethan Chu: on the success criteria side — we have three metrics: 95th p95 latency under 800ms for 512 tokens, cost under $X per 1k tokens (we'll fill in), and accuracy at parity with our baseline summarizer where f1 doesn't drop more than 2 points, is that a reasonable start?
[02:27] Diego Ramos: sounds fair, we usually run everything against your eval prompts in staging and produce a cost/latency/quality matrix — i'll propose two quantization profiles and batching configs; one that favors latency and one that favors cost,
[02:40] Maria Lopez: do you support model pinning and gradual rollouts? we want to test canary vs full flip, and rollback if quality regresses,
[02:50] Alex Mercer: definitely, rollouts are supported — canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to a smaller model variant if there's capacity stress, we'll share a rollout playbook,
[02:58] Jon Park: okay on KMS — we use a managed cloud kms and we'd prefer bring‑your‑own‑key integration, how does key rotation and audit logging look?
[03:08] Diego Ramos: BYOK is supported for Private deployments — key rotation is orchestrated by your KMS, we just reference the key aliases, audit logs include key usage entries, though in Dedicated hosted mode there's a managed key option, i'll send specifics,
[03:20] Maria Lopez: and SOC2? we need controls evidence for legal, also data residency for eu workloads?
[03:28] Priya Kaur: we have a SOC2 package and ISO documents, and region specific hosting — i'll drop the security pack, and we can redline any compliance appendix with legal,
[03:35] Ethan Chu: timeline — we want staging by early next week if possible, is that feasible?
[03:41] Alex Mercer: we'll be aggressive, priya can you call out the earliest window?
[03:45] Priya Kaur: i'll aim to have runbook + peering template to you by 2025‑04‑20, diego and i can schedule the staging window for the week of 2025‑04‑28 — that gives you time to provide IAM and test dataset,
[03:57] Jon Park: ok jon — we'll aim to share CIDR, SAML metadata and test credentials by 2025‑04‑23,
[04:04] Maria Lopez: we have a 10k doc corpus we'll anonymize and send as the staging corpus, timing is tight but doable,
[04:12] Diego Ramos: perfect, for the benchmark i'll need sample prompts and the anonymized dataset, plus expected batch sizes; we'll run a few passes: single‑request latency, steady‑state throughput at 200 concurrent streams, and cost simulation,
[04:27] Alex Mercer: quick note on telemetry — console has token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency so you'll be able to attribute cost to features,
[04:36] Ethan Chu: do you provide alerting for regressions on quality? we have automation to gate releases,
[04:42] Diego Ramos: yes, quality regression alerts tie to eval sets and we can integrate with your existing alerting via webhook or pager duty,
[04:49] Maria Lopez: any gotchas with KV cache if we do long context summaries? our queries often reference long histories,
[04:56] Diego Ramos: KV cache is supported, the runtime manages caches per session and we ofer prefix caching — small note, sometimes transcripts or docs show as "KV cash" in auto‑notes, so watch spelling in the runbook,
[05:09] Jon Park: ha noted, on networking again, what's the recommended MTU or packet size tuning for grpc streams? we've had issues with fragmentation on some infra,
[05:18] Diego Ramos: default is standard MTU, but we recommend tuning if you see fragmentation; streaming over 443 tends to work, we can share performance knobs,
[05:26] Alex Mercer: switches over to a brief commercial alignment — since this is a pilot we can propose a time‑limited trial credit and an SOW for dedicated pilot capacity if you want guaranteed throughput,
[05:38] Maria Lopez: would like a dedicated pool for the pilot if pricing and SLA make sense, to avoid noisy neighbor issues,
[05:44] Priya Kaur: we can propose a small reserved pool for the pilot and include burst policies, i'll follow up with pricing options,
[05:51] Ethan Chu: ok and for the staging environment are there limits on concurrent sessions we should expect compared to prod?
[05:58] Diego Ramos: staging mirrors prod but with scoped capacity; we'll size the pool per your concurrency targets; for the benchmark we'll propose a profile that matches your 200 concurrent streams target,
[06:09] Maria Lopez: legal will want data deletion proof after pilot ends, is there a documented retention delete flow?
[06:16] Alex Mercer: yes we have documented retention workflows and deletion APIs, priya will include references in the security pack,
[06:22] Jon Park: what about log access — can we forward logs into our existing ELK stack or do you provide read‑only exports?
[06:29] Diego Ramos: logs can be shipped via forwarders or S3 exports; for Private you can keep logs in your tenancy, for Dedicated we provide export hooks,
[06:37] Ethan Chu: i'm also curious about model updates — do you allow pinned versions per route so we don't get unexpected model changes in the middle of pilot?
[06:45] Alex Mercer: yes pinning per route and per‑customer versioning is supported; you can schedule model updates and do canary traffic,
[06:51] Maria Lopez: ok then onboarding checklist — can we walk through minimal items now so we don't miss anything?
[06:58] Priya Kaur: sure, minimal items: 1) SSO/SAML metadata and initial user list, 2) VPC peering config + CIDR, 3) anonymized test dataset and eval prompts, 4) target success metrics, 5) legal contact for SOC2 redline, 6) list of endpoints and routes you plan to use,
[07:18] Jon Park: we'll own 1 & 2, maria will handle 3 & 4 with product, legal will assign contact by friday,
[07:25] Diego Ramos: great i'll prepare the staging runbook which includes exact api routes, sample cURLs, and recommended batch sizes for each model size,
[07:34] Maria Lopez: can you provide sample cURLs that show streaming and function calling usage? we plan to use tool‑call style structured outputs for some features,
[07:42] Diego Ramos: yes — we'll include function/tool calling examples; streaming examples too, note that function calling sometimes gets auto‑transcribed as "function calling, uh toolking" in early notes,
[07:52] Alex Mercer: funny, ok — questions from axiomwave?
[07:56] Ethan Chu: do we need to sign any extra contracts for Private deployment?
[08:01] Priya Kaur: yes there is a private deployment appendix in the enterprise agreement; for on‑prem we also have an installation SOW, i'll loop legal in,
[08:10] Jon Park: curious about observability retention — logs and traces retention windows, can we configure retention length?
[08:16] Diego Ramos: observability retention is configurable for enterprise tiers; you can increase retention for an add‑on, and we provide token‑level attribution and trace links,
[08:25] Maria Lopez: ok that covers the top items for now, any idea how long the staging benchmark will take once you have the data?
[08:31] Diego Ramos: end‑to‑end benchmark runs ~1–2 business days once we have the dataset and sample prompts; we'll run multiple passes across quantization settings,
[08:40] Priya Kaur: we'll block a follow up 1 hour window to review the benchmark results and a 30‑minute alignment with legal, proposed dates week of 2025‑04‑28,
[08:50] Alex Mercer: sounds good — last bit, i'll share a spreadsheet template to capture latency/cost/quality for each run so we can compare,
[08:58] Ethan Chu: note to self: update stakeholders and prepare product brief for mid pilot demo,
[09:04] Maria Lopez: quick incidental: do you support ephemeral keys for short lived test creds? we prefer not to use long‑lived tokens for staging,
[09:12] Diego Ramos: yes ephemeral tokens via STS are supported, we'll include an example in the runbook,
[09:17] Jon Park: on peering, we'll need an endpoint IP list for the staging region — can you provide that per region?
[09:24] Priya Kaur: yes, i'll include per‑region endpoints and a CIDR mapping doc,
[09:29] Alex Mercer: ok we are at about 30 minutes, want to open to any other risk items?
[09:33] Maria Lopez: only one — we need encryption in transit and at rest verification for regulators,
[09:38] Diego Ramos: encryption both in‑flight and at rest is supported; we'll provide the certs and control plane details in the security pack,
[09:45] Ethan Chu: can you include an example incident runbook for model quality regressions? we need to show how we roll back in the ticketing system,
[09:51] Priya Kaur: yes, rollback playbook and a sample incident ticket template will be included,
[09:56] Maria Lopez: great, thanks all — anything else from the redwood side?
[10:00] Alex Mercer: nope, thanks everyone — recap: redwood to share runbook, network checklist, security pack and pricing options; axiomwave to share CIDR, SAML, anon dataset and success criteria; follow‑up benchmark week of 2025‑04‑28.
[10:14] Jon Park: confirmed from our side, we'll send the items by 2025‑04‑23,
[10:18] Ethan Chu: i'll schedule the internal stakeholder update once we have the runbook,
[10:22] Priya Kaur: i'll set the follow up meeting and send calendar invite for the benchmark review,
[10:26] Alex Mercer: thanks all, talk soon — bye,
[10:29] All: bye

End of transcript.
